subject: Re: Immediate: EdgeCraft production latency & 502 spike — suspected egress/proxy ACL
messages:
From: Amelia Fox <amelia@edgecraft.io>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 09:12:03 -0700
Subject: Production: sudden p95 latency + 502s since 09:00 — urgent

Team,

We're seeing a sharp increase in 5xxs and p95 latency across our checkout and search endpoints that call Redwood's hosted inference. The first spike started ~09:00 PDT and has persisted with intermittent recovery. Metrics:
- Error rate: rose from ~0.2% baseline to 6.8% (502/504)
- p50/p95 token latency: 75ms / 1.2s (previously 40ms / 120ms)
- Throughput drop: 18% overall on retrieval flows

We've attached a short graph and a snippet of proxy logs where you can see repeated connection resets and DNS timeouts referenced. We suspect something in the egress path / proxy ACL side — several SYNs from your egress IPs are being rejected at our firewall around the same timestamps.

Can you confirm immediately that there were no recent rolling changes to proxy ACLs, VPC peering, or DNS TTLs on Redwood's side? Need a bridge in the next 30 minutes — our execs are already briefing internal stakeholders.

Attachments: edgecraft_latency_graph.png, proxy-logs-snippet.txt

Thanks,
Amelia Fox
Head of Platform Ops, EdgeCraft
amelia@edgecraft.io
ops@edgecraft.io

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 09:26:11 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden p95 latency + 502s since 09:00 — urgent

Amelia / team — quick diagnostic summary from the triage bridge:

What we ran:
- Continuous curl + timing to edgecraft-api.edgecraft.io from our us-west-2 egress pool (two instances).
- DNS resolution logs for edgecraft-api.edgecraft.io across our resolver cluster.
- BGP / VPC peering health check to EdgeCraft's peered VPC endpoint.

Initial findings:
- DNS resolution latency spiked for several resolvers between 08:58–09:12 PDT — TTL lookups showed retries and timeouts (NXDOMAIN was not observed; timeouts only).
- Concurrently, we observed a subset of egress IPs hit connection resets at the remote firewall at ~09:03–09:07 PDT. Packet captures show repeated SYN then RST.
- Our side: no deliberate config rollouts were scheduled in the last 48 hours for proxy ACLs or DNS config. There was an automated cert refresh job at 03:00 PDT that completed normally.

Hypothesis: an intermediary proxy/device in EdgeCraft's upstream path applied a restrictive ACL or rate-limiting rule that started dropping our egress IPs after repeated DNS retries. That would explain both the DNS timeouts (if resolver queries were being rate-limited) and the later connection resets.

Next steps (proposed):
1) EdgeCraft operations to check firewall logs for explicit denies on our egress CIDR and share the rule snapshot.
2) If a recent ACL change is confirmed, request immediate rollback while we provision short-term routing/workaround (force traffic through alternate egress pool).
3) We'll prepare a temporary traffic-shift for your traffic to our alternate egress pool (requires a quick BGP route announcement and config change).

I'll produce a short diagnostic bundle (traceroute, tcpdump snippets, DNS query logs) and attach to the ticket in ~20 minutes.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Amelia Fox <amelia@edgecraft.io>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@enterprise-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 09:44:59 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden p95 latency + 502s since 09:00 — urgent

Thanks Sean — confirming what you found. Our firewall team pulled the ACL audit and discovered an automated policy push from a new proxy-management job at 08:55 PDT that inserted a deny for an IP range overlapping Redwood's egress CIDR (it matches the SYN->RST timestamps).

We've attached the firewall-acl-dump-1004.json showing the offending rule id: ACL-EDGE-1179.

Immediate asks from EdgeCraft ops:
- Please rollback/redact that ACL from our edge (we'll do the rollback on our side in parallel).
- If Redwood can route EdgeCraft traffic through the alternate egress pool while we validate, that would reduce customer impact.
- We will require a postmortem and root cause analysis, and we'll be opening a request for SLA credits given the user impact.

We are standing by on the bridge — execs are on standby for a quick meeting with your leadership if needed.

Amelia

Attachment: firewall-acl-dump-1004.json
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Oct 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec summary / proposed remediation for EdgeCraft outage (for approval)

Vivek / Marissa — short summary and ask:

Summary: EdgeCraft experienced a production regression on 2027-10-04 09:00 PDT due to an automated proxy-management job at their edge that pushed an ACL denying a block overlapping Redwood's egress CIDR. Result: elevated p95 latency and increased 502/504s for ~45 minutes during peak traffic.

Actions taken:
- Triage bridge and rollback coordination with EdgeCraft ops (they removed the offending rule).
- Sean produced diagnostic bundle and we moved EdgeCraft traffic to our alternate egress pool for 2 hours as a temporary mitigation.
- CS/Billing prepared customer-facing communication and a credit offer.

Recommended next steps / approvals requested:
1) Approve issuing a goodwill credit of USD 20k (proportional to MRR and SLA impact) pending legal sign-off.
2) Request Product/R&D to prioritize a mitigation: automated egress IP allowlist with health-check failover (P0).
3) Formal RCA with EdgeCraft and a joint runbook to prevent proxy ACL cross-over (Ops -> Product sync).

Rationale: this is a strategic customer (deal DC-4321) with significant ARR. Offering a credit and a clear technical mitigation reduces churn risk.

If approved I'll coordinate a short exec sync with EdgeCraft next week and finalize the customer-facing postmortem.

—Tessa Morgan
Account Lead, Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference
